inputs: public primary sources: Koning & van Meer 2026; Fagerland et al. 2013; Waudby-Smith & Ramdas 2024
actions: Derived explicit fixed-rho backward dynamic program for a fixed-N one-sided exact conditional McNemar terminal test.

Proved the naive same-terminal-test composite lower envelope is exactly zero on any interim state whose current no-more-discordance terminal outcome is nonrejecting, because rho->0 removes future discordances.
Numerically checked representative N=50 states and quantified nontrivial simple-rho values versus zero composite infimum.

Constructed a valid P_rho-specific terminal-test top-up family showing that the same terminal composite McNemar test can induce a different nonzero interim path, hence the composite sequentialization is nonunique.
Scoped the zero-degeneracy result rather than overgeneralizing it; identified P-specific family selection/utility as the live design problem.
material_findings: Terminal-test equivalence does not guarantee useful early-path behavior under composite nuisance parameters.

The naive exact-McNemar composite induction can have zero pre-rejection progress, but that zero path is not unique: valid P-specific decompositions can change the interim process while preserving the identical terminal composite test.
Therefore the P-specific decomposition/utility is part of the evaluation method and must itself be meta-evaluated.

termination.reason: automation turn boundary after durable checkpoint/readback; frontier intentionally remains nonempty

exact_next_action: Formulate and solve a finite-state optimization for P_rho-specific terminal-test families under N=10-50, then compare optimized induced paths with direct forward sign betting under matched terminal and Type-I constraints.
